answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so creating aliases does not create cheap voting power. If k coordinated identities equivocate on the same consensus decision, correlated penalties scale as O(k^2), while detection applies an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s capital loss and accelerates asymmetric depreciation. Thus a tide of forged votes consumes the attacker’s escrow faster than it expands influence; the kernel can quarantine linked actors, making every voyage of collusion economically self-defeating.
